lucknow.name: Lucknow
lucknow.state_eyebrow: WELCOME TO THE CITY OF NAWABS
lucknow.tagline: Nawabi heritage, Awadhi cuisine & timeless tehzeeb
lucknow.tip: Hire an official guide at Bara Imambara to explore the labyrinthine Bhool Bhulaiya, and don't miss evening chaat at Hazratganj.
lucknow.about: Lucknow, the historic capital of Uttar Pradesh along the Gomti River, is globally celebrated for its refined Awadhi tehzeeb (etiquette), courtly poetry, classical kathak dance, delicate Chikankari hand-embroidery, and an unmatched culinary repertoire developed by the Nawabs of Awadh. From the soaring Rumi Darwaza to the quiet avenues of Hazratganj, every corner tells a story of royal grandeur.
lucknow.places: Bara Imambara & Bhool Bhulaiya, Rumi Darwaza, Chhota Imambara, The British Residency, Hazratganj, Dilkusha Kothi, Ambedkar Memorial Park
lucknow.food: Tunday Galawati Kebab, Awadhi Dum Biryani, Basket Chaat at Royal Cafe, Malai Makkhan (Nimish), Sheermal, Prakash Ki Kulfi
lucknow.shopping: Chikankari Kurtas & Sarees, Zardozi embroidered fabrics, Natural Attar Perfumes at Chowk, Aminabad bazaars
lucknow.culture: Famed for Awadhi tehzeeb, Hindustani classical music, kathak dance gharanas, Urdu literature, and warm hospitality.
lucknow.history: Under Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula, Lucknow became the cultural capital of northern India in the late 18th century. It later became an epicentre of the 1857 First War of Independence, centered around the historic British Residency.
lucknow.nature: The scenic Gomti Riverfront, Janeshwar Mishra Park (one of Asia's largest eco-parks), and green boulevard gardens.
lucknow.why_visit: Experience magnificent Nawabi monuments, savor India's most celebrated kebabs and biryanis, and shop for authentic handmade Chikankari textiles.

transport.rail_summary: Lucknow is a premier railway hub with the majestic Charbagh Station (LKO / LJN) and modernized Gomti Nagar Terminal (GTNR), offering direct Vande Bharat, Tejas, and Shatabdi express trains across India.
transport.air_summary: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport (Amausi - LKO) operates high-frequency domestic and international flights, integrated directly with the Lucknow Metro Red Line.
transport.road_summary: Agra-Lucknow Expressway (3.5 hrs to Agra) and Purvanchal Expressway start here. World-class Alambagh ISBT connects to all 75 districts.
transport.local_summary: Lucknow Metro Red Line connects Airport to Munshi Pulia (23 km). E-rickshaws, city electric buses, and app cabs are available 24x7.

lucknow.trip_plan_1day: Morning: Explore Bara Imambara and Bhool Bhulaiya; drive past Rumi Darwaza. Afternoon: Savor authentic Galawati Kebabs at Tunday Kababi in Chowk. Evening: Stroll Hazratganj, enjoy basket chaat at Royal Cafe, and finish with Prakash Ki Kulfi.
lucknow.trip_plan_2day: Day 1: Old Lucknow monuments, Chhota Imambara, Clock Tower, and old city food trail. Day 2: Walk through the historic British Residency ruins, visit the State Museum, shop for Chikankari at Janpath, and relax at Gomti Riverfront.

ayodhya.name: Ayodhya
ayodhya.state_eyebrow: WELCOME TO THE SACRED BIRTHPLACE OF LORD RAMA
ayodhya.tagline: Ram Janmabhoomi, ancient temples & holy Sarayu ghats
ayodhya.fee: Temple Darshan: Free (Book Aarti passes online)
ayodhya.tip: Book your Sugam Darshan and Aarti passes in advance on the official Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra portal.
ayodhya.about: Ayodhya, situated along the sacred Sarayu River, is venerated as the birthplace of Lord Rama and one of the seven most sacred Hindu cities (Sapta Puri). With the magnificent Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, redeveloped Ram Ki Paidi ghats, and modern airport connectivity, Ayodhya is welcoming millions of pilgrims and cultural travelers from around the world.
ayodhya.places: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan, Ram Ki Paidi, Nageshwarnath Temple, Dashrath Mahal, Guptar Ghat
ayodhya.food: Ayodhya Khurchan Peda, Chandrakala, Satvik Thali, Bedhai-Jalebi, Rabri-Malai, Sweet Lassi
ayodhya.shopping: Ram Darbar brass statues, Sarayu holy water containers, Carved wooden mementos, Devotional books
ayodhya.culture: Centuries of Ramayana chanting, evening Sarayu Maha Aarti, devotional bhajan traditions, and Diwali Deepotsav.
ayodhya.history: Mentioned in the Atharvaveda and the Ramayana as the capital of the Ikshvaku dynasty. Ayodhya has been an enduring spiritual centre for millennia, also sacred in Jain tradition as the birthplace of five Tirthankaras.
ayodhya.nature: The sacred, flowing Sarayu riverfront, Ram Ki Paidi lagoons, and tranquil gardens along Guptar Ghat.
ayodhya.why_visit: Visit for darshan at the magnificent Ram Mandir, witness the mesmerizing Sarayu Aarti, and experience deep spiritual peace.

transport.air_summary: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport Ayodhya Dham (AYJ) connects with direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Ahmedabad.

transport.local_summary: Eco-friendly zero-emission travel: 200+ electric golf carts, electric buses, and battery e-rickshaws operate on Ram Path and Bhakti Path.

ayodhya.trip_plan_1day: Morning: Holy dip at Ram Ki Paidi; darshan at Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir. Afternoon: Visit Hanuman Garhi and Kanak Bhawan; enjoy traditional Satvik lunch. Evening: Mesmerizing Sarayu Maha Aarti at Naya Ghat and night walk on illuminated Ram Path.
ayodhya.trip_plan_2day: Day 1: Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan, and Sarayu Aarti. Day 2: Visit Dashrath Mahal, Sita Ki Rasoi, Nageshwarnath Temple, Ram Katha Museum, and sunset at peaceful Guptar Ghat.

varanasi.name: Varanasi
varanasi.state_eyebrow: WELCOME TO THE SPIRITUAL CAPITAL OF INDIA
varanasi.tagline: Sacred Ganga ghats, Kashi Vishwanath & timeless living traditions
varanasi.tip: Witness the morning Subah-e-Banaras from a sunrise wooden boat, and attend the evening Ganga Aarti from Dashashwamedh Ghat.
varanasi.about: Varanasi (also called Kashi and Banaras) is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in human history. Resting along the crescent curve of the sacred Ganga, it is celebrated for its 84 stone ghats, the gilded dome of Kashi Vishwanath Temple, world-famous handwoven Banarasi silk sarees, Indian classical music traditions, and unmatched street food.
varanasi.places: Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Dashashwamedh Ghat, Assi Ghat, Manikarnika Ghat, Sarnath (Buddhist deer park), Banaras Hindu University, Ramnagar Fort
varanasi.food: Kachori-Sabzi at Ram Bhandar, Tamatar Chaat at Kashi Chaat, Malaiyo (winter), Banarasi Maghai Paan, Blue Lassi, Saffron Thandai
varanasi.shopping: Handwoven Banarasi Silk Sarees, Brass idols, Gulabi Meenakari jewelry, Hand-carved wooden toys
varanasi.culture: The spiritual heart of Hinduism and Buddhism; birthplace of classical music maestros (Bismillah Khan, Ravi Shankar), and daily Vedic rituals.
varanasi.history: Mark Twain famously wrote that Varanasi is older than history, older than tradition, older even than legend. Sarnath nearby is where Gautama Buddha taught his first sermon in 528 BCE.
varanasi.nature: The majestic Ganga River, sunrise riverfront boat cruises, and the green deer parks of Sarnath.
varanasi.why_visit: Experience transformative spirituality on the ghats, hear evening temple bells, taste iconic street chaat, and acquire heirloom Banarasi silks.

varanasi.trip_plan_2day: Day 1: Ghats, Kashi Vishwanath corridor, silk markets, and evening Ganga Aarti. Day 2: Sarnath Buddhist pilgrimage (Dhamek Stupa and Museum), Banaras Hindu University, and sunset at Ramnagar Fort.

agra.name: Agra
agra.state_eyebrow: WELCOME TO THE CITY OF THE TAJ
agra.tagline: Taj Mahal, imperial Mughal forts & world-famous Petha
agra.distance: Delhi: 215 km (2.5 hrs via Yamuna Expressway)
agra.tip: Book Taj Mahal tickets online on the ASI portal (asi.payumoney.com). Remember the Taj Mahal is CLOSED on Fridays for general visitors!
agra.about: Agra on the banks of the Yamuna was the celebrated capital of the Mughal Empire during the reigns of Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. It is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal—the world's most breathtaking monument to love, the imposing red sandstone Agra Fort, and nearby Fatehpur Sikri. With the Yamuna Expressway and high-speed Gatimaan Express, it is easily visited from Delhi.
agra.places: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Mehtab Bagh (sunset view), Fatehpur Sikri, Tomb of I'timad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj), Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra
agra.food: Agra Petha (Kesar, Angoori, Paan), Bedai & Dubki Wale Aloo, Mughlai Kebabs, Dalmoth, Deviram Jalebis
agra.shopping: Panchhi Petha, Marble Inlay Souvenirs (Pietra Dura), Sadar Bazaar handcrafted leather shoes & jackets
agra.culture: Mughal court architecture, Persian garden designs, master stonecraft artisans, and festive Taj Mahotsav.
agra.history: Transformed into a grand imperial metropolis by Mughal emperors. Shah Jahan constructed the Taj Mahal between 1632 and 1648 as the mausoleum for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal.
agra.nature: Yamuna riverfront vistas, the lush Mughal gardens of Mehtab Bagh, and Sur Sarovar Bird Sanctuary.
agra.why_visit: Stand before the wonder of the Taj Mahal, wander through palatial royal courtyards, and taste sweet saffron petha made nowhere else.

prayagraj.name: Prayagraj
prayagraj.state_eyebrow: WELCOME TO THE SACRED TRIVENI SANGAM
prayagraj.tagline: Triveni Sangam confluence, Kumbh Mela & historic landmarks
prayagraj.best_time: October to March (Magh Mela in Jan-Feb)
prayagraj.tip: Hire an authorized boat to the exact confluence where the distinct colors of Ganga and Yamuna merge.
prayagraj.about: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) rests at the sacred Triveni Sangam—the confluence of the sacred Ganga, Yamuna, and mythical underground Saraswati. Revered in ancient scriptures as Prayag (king of pilgrimage sites), it hosts the monumental Kumbh Mela and Magh Mela gatherings, and preserves prominent colonial and independence-era history at Anand Bhavan.
prayagraj.places: Triveni Sangam, Anand Bhavan, Allahabad Fort & Akshayavat, Khusro Bagh, All Saints Cathedral, Bade Hanuman Ji Temple
prayagraj.food: Allahabadi Guava (Surkha), Kachori-Sabzi, Samosa, Dehati Rasgulla, Rabri-Jalebi, Netram Ki Thali
prayagraj.shopping: Religious souvenirs, Hindi and Urdu literature, Khadi garments, Fresh seasonal red guavas
prayagraj.culture: A powerhouse of Indian spiritual gatherings, national freedom movement heritage, and prestigious Hindi literary traditions.
prayagraj.history: Mentioned in the Vedas and Mahabharata. In 1583, Akbar built the formidable Allahabad Fort on the Yamuna. Later, it was the home of the Nehru family and a nerve centre of India's freedom struggle.
prayagraj.nature: The vast sandbanks and wide open waters at the Triveni Sangam, plus the green orchards of Khusro Bagh.
prayagraj.why_visit: Take a sacred boat ride to the confluence, explore Anand Bhavan's freedom struggle museum, and experience the energy of the sacred Kumbh.

prayagraj.trip_plan_2day: Day 1: Triveni Sangam, Allahabad Fort, Bade Hanuman Temple, and Civil Lines dining. Day 2: Anand Bhavan, All Saints Cathedral (Gothic architecture), Khusro Bagh, and local sweet tasting.
